gui.app.subtitle: Tune OpenTabletDriver to your hand

gui.area.subtitle: In pink, the recommended area to scale; it maps onto your whole screen.
gui.area.title: Your area on the tablet
gui.baseline.intro: Before changing anything we take two quick measurements with your current settings, so we can tell whether a new setting is really better. Make sure OpenTabletDriver is running and your pen moves the cursor. Each test takes a few seconds.
gui.baseline.skip_note: You can skip these tests, but the suggestions will then be more generic.
gui.baseline.title: Your starting point
gui.change.area_kept: Your tablet area stays the same.
gui.change.area_larger: Your area goes from {old_w} x {old_h} mm to {w} x {h} mm: {pct}% bigger. You move your hand more, in exchange for more control.
gui.change.area_moved: The area moves on the tablet (its center is now at {x}, {y} mm).
gui.change.area_same: The area size stays practically the same ({w} x {h} mm).
gui.change.area_smaller: Your area goes from {old_w} x {old_h} mm to {w} x {h} mm: {pct}% smaller. The same hand movement covers more screen (faster cursor).
gui.change.filters_kept: Your filters stay as they are.
gui.change.filters_none: No filters, same as now: direct input.
gui.change.filters_removed_all: All filters are removed: the cursor follows the pen with no smoothing.
gui.change.latency: The filters add an estimated delay of about {ms} ms.

gui.close.title: Close the assistant
gui.community.note: Their values are adapted to your area for the comparison. A different value is not a mistake: what matters is what measured best for you.
gui.community.subtitle: Your result next to the closest published setups: what differs, where it comes from and how reliable it is.
gui.community.title: Compared with community setups
gui.compare.empty: There are no measurements to compare yet. Try an option to see the difference.
gui.compare.note: "Before" uses your measured current setup (or your starting tests). Small differences may just be measurement noise.
gui.compare.subtitle: Your current setup against the recommended one. Shorter bar = better.
gui.compare.title: Before and after

gui.display.width_help: Horizontal resolution of the monitor you play on.
gui.filters.col.name: Filter / parameter
gui.filters.none: No filters: the cursor follows the pen directly, with the least delay.
gui.filters.subtitle: Applied in this order, with exactly these values.
gui.filters.title: Filter chain
gui.howto.cancel: Each test takes a few seconds. Press Esc to cancel it at any time.
gui.howto.hover: In the aim test, each circle counts as soon as the cursor enters it: just move over it.
gui.howto.no_clicks: No clicking needed: just move the pen. You can touch the tablet or keep the pen in the air, very close to the surface (hovering).
gui.howto.short: The tests need no clicks: move the pen touching the tablet or hovering. The results measure your speed and how steady the cursor is.
gui.howto.speed: The results mainly measure speed: how fast you reach each target and how well the cursor keeps up with your hand. Play at your normal pace, don't force it.
gui.howto.title: How the tests work
gui.preset.intro: You can start from a ready-made preset. The assistant uses it as a base and compares it with its own suggestions.
gui.preset.no_source: provided by you, no public source
gui.preset.none: None: start with the assistant's suggestions
gui.preset.note: Published setups are starting points: the one you pick is measured first and compared with the assistant's own options. Millimetre values are adapted to your area (a heuristic, shown in the reasons). Only setups whose plugins are allowed by your plugin choice are listed.
gui.preset.title: Pick a starting point
gui.questions.intro: These answers help choose sensible starting settings. Nothing here is permanent.
gui.questions.keep_area.label: Keep my current area width ({width} mm)
gui.questions.keep_area.title: Keep your current area size?
gui.questions.keep_area.why: Why we ask: if you already like how big your area feels, we keep its width and only adjust the rest.
gui.questions.map_preference.title: What kind of maps do you play most?
gui.questions.map_preference.why: Why we ask: jump maps reward precise long moves; stream maps need a very steady cursor.
gui.questions.notices_input_lag.label: Yes, the cursor feels like it lags behind my hand
gui.questions.notices_input_lag.title: Do you feel input lag?
gui.questions.notices_input_lag.why: Why we ask: if the cursor feels late, we avoid options that add delay.
gui.questions.notices_jitter.label: Yes, I see the cursor shaking when I hold the pen still
gui.questions.notices_jitter.title: Does your cursor shake?
gui.questions.notices_jitter.why: Why we ask: if you see tremor while holding the pen still, we give noise reduction more weight.
gui.questions.play_style.title: How do you move the pen?
gui.questions.play_style.why: Why we ask: big arm movements need a larger tablet area; finger and wrist aiming work better with a smaller one.
gui.questions.plugin_policy.allow_new_he: Also lists plugins you do not have, with the reason, where to get them and how to install them yourself.
gui.questions.plugin_policy.installed_he: It may pick among the plugins found in OpenTabletDriver's Plugins folder.
gui.questions.plugin_policy.title: Which plugins may the assistant use?
gui.questions.plugin_policy.tune_only_he: Your filters and their order stay. Only their values change, one at a time, each shown as current value -> proposed value with the reason.
gui.questions.plugin_policy.why: Why we ask: some players want to keep their filters and only fine-tune them. The assistant never installs plugins itself.
gui.questions.priority.title: What matters more to you?
gui.questions.priority.why: Why we ask: filters can make the cursor smoother, but most of them add a tiny delay.
gui.questions.skill_level.title: How experienced are you?
gui.questions.skill_level.why: Why we ask: beginners usually benefit from more smoothing; experienced players tend to prefer raw, direct input.
gui.questions.title: About you

gui.tip.area: Area: the part of the tablet that maps to your screen. A smaller area makes the cursor faster (less hand movement); a bigger one gives more control.
gui.tip.chatter: Chatter: small jumps or vibrations of the cursor when the pen is almost still, caused by sensor noise. "Antichatter" filters dampen them.
gui.tip.jitter: Jitter: how much the cursor moves on its own while you hold the pen still. Measured in tablet millimetres; lower is better.
gui.tip.latency: Added delay (latency): how many milliseconds a filter makes the cursor trail your hand. It is an estimate based on each filter's documentation.
gui.tip.plugins: Plugins add filters to OpenTabletDriver (smoothing, antichatter, resampling). Prediction plugins are never turned on automatically because of osu!'s rules on input assistance.
gui.tip.report_rate: Report rate: how many positions per second the tablet sends to the computer. Higher = smoother movement and slightly less delay.
gui.tip.smoothing: Smoothing: filters that average pen positions to remove cursor shake. The more they smooth, the more delay they add.
gui.tip.tablet_list:
Active area: the size of the usable surface of the tablet, in millimetres.
Reports/s (report rate): how many positions per second the tablet sends.
gui.welcome.disclaimer: This assistant gives measured, explainable starting points, not a guaranteed perfect setting: every hand and every tablet is different, and you can keep fine-tuning afterwards. Before it changes anything it always makes a backup of your OpenTabletDriver settings, and it only applies something when you confirm.
gui.welcome.dry_run: Dry-run mode is on: nothing will be applied to OpenTabletDriver. You will only get a preset file and a report.
gui.welcome.intro: This assistant helps you set up OpenTabletDriver for osu!. It looks at your tablet, asks a few questions, tries some settings while you move your pen, and suggests the tablet area and filters that work best for you.
gui.welcome.step1: We find OpenTabletDriver and your tablet (read-only, nothing is changed).
gui.welcome.step2: You tell us how you play.
gui.welcome.step3: You do a few short tests just by moving the pen, no clicks (a few seconds each).
gui.welcome.step4: We try several settings, measure them and recommend the best one.
gui.welcome.step5: You decide whether to save it as a preset or apply it.
gui.welcome.title: Welcome
gui.welcome.what_happens:
What will happen:
1. We find OpenTabletDriver and your tablet.
2. You tell us how you play.
3. You do a few short pen tests (a few seconds each).
4. We try some settings, measure them and suggest the best one.
5. You decide whether to save it or apply it.
